title: operator-skill-matrix-and-microlearning-path-2026
author: Maya Gupta
body:
Overview:

This page describes a repeatable operator skill matrix and a complementary microlearning pathway for Platform Operators at Redwood Inference. The goal is to reduce mean time to competency for new operators, formalize role expectations for escalation/triage, and create a measurable training loop that feeds into oncall readiness checks and quarterly certification.

Why this exists:
- Operators shoulder the day-to-day health of the inference platform: routing, caching, autoscaling, and fallback policies.
- Existing onboarding is effective but ad-hoc; we need a lightweight, continuous training approach that fits 15–30 minute slots.
- Microlearning + scenario-based assessments have shown faster retention vs long instructor-led sessions for operational skills.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: Platform Operators, Platform SREs, Platform Oncall Deputies, and Engineering ICs rotating onto oncall.
- Scope: Core operator competencies for eng-platform systems (traffic shepherding, prefix cache, batching, model variant fallbacks, emergency model swap). Not a substitute for deep runtime or kernel-level training.

Skill levels (definition):
1) Familiar: Has observed the workflow and can read the runbook; may need guidance for hands-on steps.
2) Practicing: Can execute common procedures under supervision; can triage known alerts with checklist.
3) Autonomous: Independently executes runbooks, runs canary experiments, and authors small playbook changes.
4) Mentor: Teaches others, designs scenario tests, owns runbook revisions for complex subsystems.

Operator competency matrix (summary table):
- Traffic shaping and tenant prioritization: Familiar | Practicing | Autonomous | Mentor
- KV/prefix cache failure triage: Familiar | Practicing | Autonomous | Mentor
- Model variant fallback and emergency-swap: Familiar | Practicing | Autonomous | Mentor
- Predictive batching and fairness tuning: Familiar | Practicing | Autonomous | Mentor
- Observability & SLI debugging (token-level traces): Familiar | Practicing | Autonomous | Mentor
- Incident comms and stakeholder triage: Familiar | Practicing | Autonomous | Mentor

(Full matrix with criteria available in the linked certification sheet.)

Microlearning pathway (modular schedule):
- Phase 0: Pre-reqs (self-paced, ~1 hour)
  - Permissions & tooling checklist (Slack, PagerDuty, Grafana, VictoriaMetrics read-only)
  - Quick read: "Platform operator basics" (10 min)
- Module A: Alert-to-Triage (15 minutes)
  - Objective: From alert to triage in 15 minutes.
  - Content: Short video walkthrough + 3-step checklist.
  - Assessment: 5-item multiple choice.
- Module B: Prefix-cache hotpath (20 minutes)
  - Objective: Identify cache misrouting vs eviction storms and execute safe warmup.
  - Content: Guided terminal lab (playground tenant) with sample PromQL and example logs.
  - CLI snippets: "redwoodctl cache inspect --tenant=dev-playground"
- Module C: Model fallback and canary swap (25 minutes)
  - Objective: Perform a canary model swap and verify rollback.
  - Content: YAML example for rollout policy and short runbook extract.
  - Example rollout fragment:
    rollout_policy:
      canary_percent: 5
      watch_sli: token_latency_p50
      rollback_on: p999_latency > 2s
- Module D: Token-cost forensics & mitigation (20 minutes)
  - Objective: Find token leak sources and apply soft-quotas.
  - Content: Dashboard tour + triage template.
- Module E: Degraded-region failover (30 minutes)
  - Objective: Execute manual region failover and rehydrate routing.
  - Assessment: Practical scenario in synthetic lab.

Assessment and certification flow:
1) Weekly microlearning cadence for new hires during first 6 weeks.
2) Short quizzes after each module; pass threshold 80%.
3) Week 6: Hands-on scenario (30–45 minutes) observed by mentor; scenario includes a prefix cache eviction + model misroute.
4) Certification record updated in the operator ledger.
5) Quarterly recertification: 1-hour lab + updated quiz (focus on recent platform changes).

Runbook integration and versioning:
- All modules reference canonical runbooks in /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks.
- Runbooks are the source of truth for procedural steps; microlearning modules extract focused snippets.
- Versioning: training modules carry a "runbook-version" tag that matches the runbook last_updated date. Operators must re-run affected modules when runbook major version increments.

Metrics and success criteria (how we measure impact):
- Mean time to competency (target): 8 weeks -> 4–6 weeks after rollout.
- Mean time to acknowledgement and triage for top-10 alerts (10% reduction target in 3 months).
- Oncall error rate attributable to personnel (post-incident operator mistakes) reduced by 30% in 6 months.
- Certification coverage: 90% of active operators certified within 3 months of program rollout.

Implementation plan (quarterly roadmap snippets):
- Q4 2025: Pilot with 6 operators; complete Modules A–C; gather feedback. Owner: Platform Training Guild.
- Q1 2026: Expand to full operator population; add Modules D–E; integrate quizzes into LMS. Owner: Eng-Platform Learning.
- Q2 2026: Add scenario generator and synthetic lab automation for hands-on assessments. Owner: SRE Tools team.
- Q3 2026: Begin cross-team exercises with product on real canaries; measure SLO changes. Owner: Platform Ops.

Owner and maintenance:
- Program owner: Platform Training Guild (contact: maya.gupta@redwood.com).
- Module authors: rotation across Platform SRE, Runtime, and Observability teams.
- Quarterly review: Guild sync to update modules after major runtime or routing changes.

Dependencies and risks:
- Requires a writable sandbox tenant for labs; risk if sandbox parity drifts from production. Mitigation: monthly sync and smoke tests.
- LMS integration: initial manual grading for practical scenarios; plan to automate pass/fail capture.
- Cultural: Operators may deprioritize microlearning during high-incident windows. Mitigation: manager-OKRs to protect learning time.

Appendix A — Sample quiz (Module A, 5 questions):
1) After receiving a 'token-latency-p90' alert for tenant X, first step is: (A) Increase burst credits (B) Perform triage by checking p50/p99 and recent deployments (C) Reboot serving nodes (D) Notify customer
2) Which dashboard panel best differentiates prefix-cache eviction vs request spike? (A) KV eviction rate (B) Token spend per request (C) NGINX errors (D) Disk I/O
3) True/False: Rolling back a model variant can be done without updating routing tables.
4) What PromQL snippet isolates tenant-specific token latency? Provide the metric name.
5) Name two SLOs you should check before approving a canary swap.

Appendix B — Example short playbook excerpt (Module C):
1) Pre-checks: Confirm canary SLI targets are green for baseline (p50 < 200ms, p999 < 2s).
2) Deploy canary at 5%. Wait 3 minutes.
3) Monitor token_latency_p50, token_latency_p999, and error_rate.
4) If p999 > 2s or error_rate increase > 0.5%: rollback.
5) If stable at 15 minutes: ramp to 25%, then 100% with staged windows.

Feedback loop and continuous improvement:
- Post-module feedback form embedded in LMS; triage responses weekly.
- Learning data (quiz scores, lab pass rates) feeds into hiring and rotation decisions.
- Runbook changes with operator friction > 5% require a training note added to the module within 2 weeks.

Contacts and next steps:
- To join the pilot or volunteer as a mentor, email maya.gupta@redwood.com.
- Next review meeting: 2026-03-15, Platform Training Guild.
